Here's what came out after a quick edit. Lightened the image up a bit, cloned/healed out the blown out areas and some of the distracting elements of the image, adjusted the colour levels to pop the fish out of the rocks, filtered out a bit of the noise, sharpened it up somewhat which also brought the fish out of the background a bit more, removed some of the bluish swirls that seemed to draw the eye away from the fish themselves, and reframed the image with a crop to remove the leaves in the upper right hand corner that seemed a bit of a distraction.

As someone who works outdoors in the Pacific Northwest, we have significant swings in amounts of daylight between winter solstice and summer solstice, I've learned that it's very important to begin exposing your skin to the sun as early as possible in the year, to include the top of your head if you don't have much hair like me. The idea is that you're building up your tolerance to sunlight while the sunlight is still coming through the atmosphere at a significant angle. By the time it's summer, your skin can handle being outside without having to worry about sunburns. While it may seem simplistic and intuitive, it's surprising how many people whom spend significant times outdoors fail to build tolerance throughout the year. As for those whom are redheads, I wish I could say this would work for you, but the cases I've seen of people trying, it always ends badly. SPF50 is a redhead's friend.

I am tired of being skinny fat or even chubby fat and I want to get into the best shape of my life starting today. What is the current opinion on the best diet and training program to get lean before even thinking about adding bulk? Is this still even the way of thinking? I am 26-years-old, 6' 215 lbs, probably 28% body fat I'd wager, and I have very little muscle mass in my arms and legs. I kind of resemble a potato.

Plz help.
Advice on diet and workout plan to cut from 25+% body fat to sub 15%?

Can only speak for myself (6'1, 180 lbs) but I've been getting reasonably good results with intermittent fasting and bodyweight exercises. Gone from way over 30 percent body fat late last year (was 240 lbs) to 18 percent now (according to navy tape measure method which has a margin of error of 3 percent) and looking to get to sub 10 by the end of the year.

Intermittent fasting seems to make it very easy and comfortable to be at a calorie deficit for the day. I stop eating at 6 or 8 at night and start eating again at 10 in the morning or midday, so I have a relatively small window to get my calories into. Currently eat between 1500 and 2000 a day depending on whether I work out or not. I usually split this up into 2 or 3 meals. I don't watch macros, but I try and eat as much protein as possible within my calorie limit to spare muscle mass.

When I work out I do an hour or two of cardio (walking/jogging) interspersed every 5 or 10 minutes with sets of 10-20 pushups, wide pushups, diamond pushups, crunches, planks, dips, squats. This has built up my strength and endurance even while eating at a calorie deficit everyday.

Im 5'10 around 165pounds Male and don't need to loose weight but in my experience intermittent fasting works best (it is a bit difficult to get into as its a big change to the way you will be used to eating.)

I generally eat 1 time a day at around 3pm, but will have about 2 cups of coffee through the day.

I have 300grams bacon 3eggs and some cheese with an avo. This meal has enough fat to keep me full for ages.

I do a lot of bodyweight stuff: Pull-ups, pushups, body rows, dips...etc (Big compound exercises) There are beginner progressions for everything if you can't do any of the bodyweight moves.

Beginner Routine but add some HIT training on off days. I like to follow paleo diet eating style.

I downloaded a calorie tracking app. Basically a food journal. I'm amazed at how freaking easy it is to maintain a calorie deficit when you track it. I've been hitting the gym for 7 months and decided to give the whole "cutting" thing a try and initially decided on a month just to see how it went. But I'm on my 3rd week. Weight is falling off with hardly any additional effort it's so easy I'm thinking of making it 2 months so I can hopefully go down a pant size.

Yeah, I count calories in my head, to get to between 1500 and 2000 kcal. Yesterday I had 1740. If I don't know how many calories something has, I google it and weigh it on my food scale. Counting calories in your head is not for everyone (you need a relatively reliable short term memory, and need to be able to get into the habit of googling and weighing things), but honestly I find it easier than calorie tracking with an app, which would take a load of effort in terms of data input. (Data input has never been my thing, although I do weigh myself every day and record the result).

Intermittent fasting is more a method to make having a calorie deficit less taxing on the mind and body. For some reason the one thing that makes me really hungry and sets off cravings is eating. And the fewer hours I allow myself to eat in, the less cravings I have. I don't know if everyone else is like this, but it seems to work for me.

Go to Amazon and order a copy of Bigger, Leaner, Stronger by Mike Matthews. He lays out the entire process from nutrition to specific workouts to mental focus. I did all the P90 type exercises and they helped me drop some weight but that book really made me get serious.

For me, it was Keto that did it. 6'4" 225 @ 25%BF -> 180 @ 11-12% BF. Recently started stronglifts 5x5 and i am very pleased with the results so far.

I'm currently 6'4", 235~240lbs and by those dinky little plastic calipers I'm at 15~17% BF. This is my normal rest state. I can drop down to 13% fairly easily (with the work/diet) but don't really get much higher. I started out in the 23~25% range a little over a decade ago and the single biggest/fastest impact that really jump-started the process was doing P90x with my wife and being a complete Nazi about the diet. As the saying goes, you lose weight in the kitchen and get fit in the gym... sounds like you want to Both lose the fat AND gain some muscle. It's also worth knowing and understanding that for long term results (the rest of your life type results), that you need to make lifestyle changes... like, not drinking your calories (no more soda, beer, wine, liquor or anything other than water really ~ just that One change, with nothing else, shed ~20lbs from my frame), also it's time to stop eating pre-prepared foods... that's fast food, anything you can eat straight out of a box/bag (there are a few exceptions), etc... My wife and I eat out about 4~5 times a year, special occasions and when there's no other option while traveling (we still cook most of our own meals while traveling/vacationing). By a recent study, 80% of weight change is done in the kitchen via what you eat and only 20% is done in the gym (though there are studies to back up anything, this one seems accurate based on my personal experiences).

It's hard to get into that kind of lifestyle, takes work. Especially if your family was anything like mine... my dad taught me to sit down with a bag of chip and finish it in one sitting, same with a bag of M&M's, or anything really. They still do that when I visit, but it's not even appealing to me anymore.

When it does come time to be active, I find doing "exercises" a drag ~ I HATE going to a specific room/place just to work my muscles. I do as much as I can outside, with sports/activities, to replace time in the gym. It helps me exercise More and tends to be better (involving more muscle groups, no isolation) for what I want out of my exercise. I'm not after some cut look, I want real world, long term, sustainable health. I'm 41 and my goal is to be in better shape next year than I am this year, which has been the same goal I've had for ~10 years now. I think I've made it every year too.

Good luck, and even if you do Nothing else to get started, get out and walk for 30 minutes today. Fitness is a culmination of lots of little changes, little changes Anyone can make/do.
